question: Can a contract-valid Unicode mission run through the provider/worker RPC boundary under a real non-UTF-8 process locale?

fixtures.ascii: Published shape, ASCII mission and payload strings.
fixtures.unicode: Same shape and rights, valid Unicode in mission ID, subject and payload labels.

failure_criterion: Both controls complete two obligations; Unicode/ASCII fails in implicit text encoding despite valid normalized contract. No authority or semantic payload mutation is introduced.
correction_scope_if_reproduced: Explicit UTF-8 bytes on RPC input/output and worker JSON output, inside probes/implementation/corrected only. Do not change existing handoff R4 parsers.
after_matrix: Repeat the six affected transport cases, plus Unicode/ASCII opaque lost-ACK for each interface; preserve UNKNOWN and no second effect after an ordinary released-lease retry.
limitations: Executed on current Linux host only; no claim that Windows was executed here.
A real ASCII locale is selected, not mocked encoding or modified code behavior.
This establishes a transport/availability defect for accepted inputs, not an authorization bypass.
